description: Public-evidence cross-checks for the toller-survey step rates. For each mapped step a bottom-up FLOOR hourly rate is derived from the installed equipment costs published in DOE/NETL-2002/1169 (Loh 2002). The floor covers annualized installed capital, fixed charges, and an attended-labor share; utilities, consumables and toller margin are deliberately excluded, so a valid toller rate must sit at or above its floor. The floors corroborate the CatCost rates without replacing them: the report's stated curve accuracy (+50%/-30%) is wider than the toller survey's, so swapping values would increase uncertainty, not reduce it.

report.citation: Loh, H.P., Lyons, J., White, C.W. III, 'Process Equipment Cost Estimation, Final Report', DOE/NETL-2002/1169, U.S. Department of Energy, National Energy Technology Laboratory, January 2002
report.local_copy: backend/data/references/DOE-NETL-2002-1169_Loh_process_equipment_cost.pdf (not committed - the repo gitignores *.pdf; re-fetch from a mirror URL if absent)
report.retrieval_note: osti.gov drops TCP connections from non-US networks (DNS and ICMP respond, port 443 is filtered); the PDF was retrieved 2026-08-28 from the Internet Archive capture of the OSTI download URL and verified against the UNT catalog metadata (410 KB, 78 pages).
report.cost_basis: 1st quarter 1998 USD (report p.3); installed costs from Appendix B include setting labor and installation bulks

method.formula: floor_usd_per_hr = installed_1998 * (cepci_2017 / cepci_1998) * (crf + maintenance_frac + taxes_frac + insurance_frac) / annual_hours + operators_per_step * labor_rate_usd_per_hr * (1 + plant_overhead_frac)
method.result_basis: mid-2017 USD/hr, matching the STEP_COSTS basis so the engine's ChemPPI escalation applies identically to rate and floor

constants.crf_note: capital recovery factor i(1+i)^n/((1+i)^n-1), the standard preliminary-estimate annualization
constants.fixed_charge_source: backend/data/opex_factors.json (M&R 5% of FCI, local taxes 2.5% of FCI, insurance 0.8% of FCI)
constants.labor_source: backend/data/opex_factors.json (direct labor $48/hr; plant overhead 60% of labor line)
constants.labor_note: one operator assumed to attend two concurrent steps

method.tier_duty_basis: small 1 t/day, medium 10 t/day, large 150 t/day at 24 h/day (backend/core/constants.py PRODUCTION_RATES, HOURS_PER_DAY)

small.sizing: 1 t/day = 42 kg/h; smallest tabulated ball mill

dryer_rotary_40_100C.maps_to: Direct contact rotary dryer (curve p.24, table p.64)

small.sizing: smallest tabulated area; 1 t/day duty sits at the curve floor, so the floor is conservative-high on capital

medium.sizing: drying area scaled with evaporative duty at 10 t/day

dryer_rotary_100_300C.maps_to: Direct contact rotary dryer (curve p.24, table p.64)
dryer_rotary_100_300C.note: same equipment points as the 40-100C band: the fuel-duty difference between the temperature bands is a utility cost, which the floor excludes by construction

medium.sizing: drying area scaled with evaporative duty at 10 t/day

dryer_batch_vacuum_tray.maps_to: Atmospheric tray batch dryer (curve p.24, table p.64)
dryer_batch_vacuum_tray.note: vacuum construction costs more than the atmospheric proxy, so the floor is conservative-low

small.sizing: 90 sq ft tray area for 1 t/day batch drying

filter_plate_frame.maps_to: Automatic plate and frame filter (curve p.26, table p.66)

small.sizing: smallest tabulated frame capacity (10 cu ft) covers 1 t/day of solids

medium.sizing: 10 t/day at the report's default 0.5 t/day per sq ft needs ~20 sq ft; smallest tabulated drum is 100 sq ft (curve floor, conservative-high)

large.sizing: 150 t/day at 0.5 t/day per sq ft needs ~300 sq ft; next tabulated size up is 500 sq ft

mixer_slurry.maps_to: Agitator + vertical vessel, 15 psig (curves p.5 and p.27, tables p.52 and p.67)

small.sizing: 1 t/day solids at ~20 wt% slurry is ~1250 gal/day, batched in a 500 gal working vessel

medium.sizing: 10 t/day slurry duty in a 5000 gal vessel

large.sizing: 150 t/day slurry duty exceeds the largest tabulated vertical vessel (5000 gal); no floor derived

incipient_wetness.maps_to: Agitator + vertical vessel, 15 psig (curves p.5 and p.27, tables p.52 and p.67)
incipient_wetness.note: liquid duty is pore volume only (~0.5-1 L per kg support), so vessels stay small relative to slurry mixing

small.sizing: 1 t/day at ~0.8 L/kg is ~210 gal/day of solution

medium.sizing: 10 t/day at ~0.8 L/kg is ~2100 gal/day, batched

large.sizing: 150 t/day at ~0.8 L/kg is ~32000 gal/day across repeated 5000 gal batches

crystallizer.maps_to: Standard vertical tube evaporator as evaporative-crystallizer body (curve p.21, table p.61)
crystallizer.note: an evaporative crystallizer is approximated by the evaporator body; internals specific to crystallization are not priced by the report

medium.sizing: heat-transfer area scaled with evaporative duty at 10 t/day

large.sizing: largest tabulated vertical-tube area at 150 t/day

unmapped_steps.kiln_continuous_indirect: no calciner or kiln among the report's 31 equipment types
unmapped_steps.dryer_spray: no spray dryer among the report's dryer types (rotary, drum, tray)
unmapped_steps.filter_belt_vacuum: no belt filter among the report's filter types
unmapped_steps.ball_forming: no forming or agglomeration equipment in the report

unmapped_steps.reactor_multistep: multi-vessel train sizing would stack unsourced assumptions; not derived
unmapped_steps.scrubber_nox: rate is attendance-dominated: the floor's fixed labor share (0.5 operator) already exceeds the small-tier rate, so the floor construction is uninformative here
unmapped_steps._proxy_steps: the nine MEA proxy steps are tracked as a separate debt in test_evidence_provenance.py and are out of scope for thermocatalyst equipment anchoring
